description:
Extend the builtin pattern of clz/ctz/popcount/mulhi (defk-52v.6): a builtin with a precise integer definition, a portable C fallback, a hardware instruction where one exists, and an Elixir-mode implementation with agreement properties.

- Start with crc32c(acc, word) for u8/u32/u64 words (ARMv8 CRC32C*, SSE4.2 crc32). Measure examples/hashes.exs CRC32C against crc32cer (today crc32cer is 14x faster than the kernel).
- Then, if the research ticket supports it: carry-less multiply (CRC32/CRC64 folding, GHASH), and possibly single AES/SHA rounds; compare with :crypto.
- Decide how a builtin picks its implementation in a portable build: only the fallback; runtime dispatch per call site (target_clones / a cached CPU-feature check); or only in an architecture build. Measure the dispatch cost.
- Devex: how the docs and errors present a builtin that is fast on one target and slow on another (docs/language.md Builtins table).

Done when crc32c is prototyped with all three implementations, agreement properties pass in both modes and under forced yields, and the speedup per target is recorded.

comments.text: Unblocked by the maintainer (2026-10-11): ulk.1's research (docs/research/simd.md) recommends this first and it doesn't depend on the outstanding x86 timings; a crc32c builtin can choose the instruction at run time, so it needs no architecture build.

Prototype done on branch defk-ulk.4/crc32c-builtin (ad6e230, merged main 47971fb, 48736d1). Not merged to main. Left OPEN: Done-when asks for the speedup per target and x86-64 is compiled only, not timed.

API: crc32c(crc, x, w), w in 8/16/32/64 (Defk.Bits.crc32c/3). One raw CRC32C step (reflected 0x82F63B78, no inversion, w/8 bytes LSB first) = exactly CRC32C{B,H,W,X} / SSE4.2 crc32{b,w,l,q}. Checked like clz/2 and rotl/3 (Defk.Bits width convention): width first, crc in 0..2^32-1, x in 0..2^w-1, else ArgumentError with Defk.Bits' message; result i64 in 0..2^32-1 (range fact for the compiler). Chosen over crc32c_u8/_u32/_u64 or crc32c(acc, word) because the width-taking builtins already exist (clz/2, rotl/3) and one name covers four instruction sizes. Cost of the convention: u64_le gives the i64 pattern, so the 64-bit word is written band(u64_le(b, i), 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF) (free; documented).

Three implementations: (1) portable C: slicing-by-8 tables (8x256 u32) built on first use under pthread_once; (2) hardware: inline asm crc32c{b,h,w,x} on aarch64 (.arch_extension crc) and crc32{b,w,l,q} on x86-64 - inline asm, not intrinsics, so it inlines into code built without the feature (GCC refuses to inline a target("+crc") function: 648 vs 400 us); the asm keeps the register 64-bit (the instruction zeroes the top half), which removed a mov w,w from the chain (536 -> 395 us); (3) Elixir: Defk.Bits.crc32c/3, byte-table, doctested; Elixir mode calls it.

Dispatch decision: runtime dispatch, always, per kernel library: a cached atomic state (0 unknown / 1 instruction / 2 table), relaxed load + predicted branch per call, set at the library's first crc32c call. Detection: __ARM_FEATURE_CRC32 or __APPLE__ -> instruction; Linux aarch64 getauxval(AT_HWCAP) & HWCAP_CRC32; x86-64 CPUID SSE4.2 (cpuid.h, no libgcc __builtin_cpu_supports dependency); other arches -> table only. Override DEFK_PORTABLE_BUILTINS=<anything but ""/"0"> read with enif_getenv (so System.put_env works; getenv does not see it) forces the table, for tests and measurement. Mod.__defk_stats__().crc32c reports :instruction | :table | :not_called. Never SIGILL: the instruction runs only after the check. No architecture build needed.
Measured dispatch cost: none. Kernel, 4 MB one chain: 0.389-0.393 ms dispatched vs 0.390-0.393 ms instruction called directly (header hacked). Plain C 389 vs 389 us (also with an opaque call per iteration). Debian GCC 14 kernel for plain armv8-a (check really runs): 0.402 ms.

CRC32C, 4 MB, examples/hashes.exs, best of 5, three runs, Apple M4 Pro, load 25-40 (PROVISIONAL), arm64 macOS:
- kernel, instruction, 3 streams (2 KB each, joined by a 4x256 shift table, as Google crc32c does): 0.147-0.165 ms (25-28 GB/s)
- kernel, table fallback (DEFK_PORTABLE_BUILTINS=1), 3 streams: 0.68-0.70 ms
- previous kernel (slicing-by-8, no builtin): 1.83-1.88 ms
- crc32cer 1.1.4: 0.134-0.140 ms -> kernel 0.84-0.91x of it (was 14x slower)
- Elixir slicing-by-8 (optimised baseline): 2.59-2.65 ms -> 17-18x, verdict good (was marginal 1.39-1.65x)
- one chain: instruction 0.39 ms, table 1.89 ms
- 1k x 32 B keys: Elixir 0.031-0.033 ms vs kernel batch 0.033-0.036 ms incl. packing (0.89-0.94x)
- Elixir 3 streams tried: 5.6-6.4 ms vs 2.57-2.59 one chain (JIT op-bound); baseline stays one chain.
arm64 Linux (Debian, GCC 14, podman VM on the same M4; not separate hardware): crc32c_test + bit_builtins_test pass, instruction picked via getauxval; 3 streams 0.194 ms, table 0.722 ms; one chain 0.402 / 1.78 ms.
x86-64: generated kernel C compiled with Apple clang -target x86_64-apple-macos13 and zig cc x86_64-linux-gnu (crc32q emitted); the runtime code's SSE4.2 path ran correctly under Rosetta 2 (not a timing). NOT timed on x86 hardware -> ticket stays open for that number (one run of examples/hashes.exs on an x86-64 Linux box; the `crc32c builtin on ...` line says which implementation ran).

Tests: test/crc32c_test.exs (edges per width vs a bitwise reference, properties vs Elixir mode for every width and for messages, error agreement, literal widths, qualified Defk.Bits.crc32c, RFC 3720 vectors, forced yields on 2 MB inputs for both libraries, the instruction vs DEFK_PORTABLE_BUILTINS library on 2000 random steps). examples/hashes.exs checks the portable library against crc32cer and Elixir mode. ci: format, compile --warnings-as-errors, test (flaky timeouts under load passed on rerun), docs, credo --strict, dialyzer, ex_dna, reach all pass.

Docs: language.md Builtins row + new "Hardware builtins" section with a per-target table (what runs, what it measured) as the answer to "fast on one target, slower on another": same value everywhere, speed table per target, __defk_stats__().crc32c, DEFK_PORTABLE_BUILTINS. Cheatsheet, Defk.Bits moduledoc, compile-errors.md regenerated (builtin list), performance.md 6.21 and 6.22, examples/README hashes row (CRC32C moved from "Elixir is right" to "defk helps").

What remains for carry-less multiply and AES/SHA rounds (not built):
- clmul(a, b) -> {lo, hi} or clmul_lo/clmul_hi(a, b): 64x64 carry-less product; PMULL/PMULL2 needs the arm64 `aes` feature (FEAT_PMULL; in the Apple default, getauxval HWCAP_PMULL on Linux), PCLMULQDQ on x86 is outside every psABI level, so it needs exactly this runtime dispatch (CPUID bit 1 of ECX). The portable fallback is a 64-step shift-xor loop or a 4-bit-window table (slow, ~10-20x the instruction), and the Elixir definition is a bitwise loop. A two-word result needs a tuple return or two builtins (a kernel cannot return a tuple from a helper today). Would let CRC-64/XZ and CRC-16 fold (geohash_crc 0.5 GB/s now) and GHASH.
- AES/SHA single rounds: aese/aesmc, sha256h/sha256su0/1, sha512h; x86 AES-NI and SHA-NI (SHA-NI not on many Intel server parts). Each needs 128-bit values (two i64 words in and out, i.e. tuple results), which is the vector-value question (defk-ulk.5). :crypto already uses these instructions, and constant-time/secret handling keeps crypto in the wrapper table, so only SHA-256 hash chains (hash_chain.exs, 0.57x :crypto) would benefit; low priority until ulk.5 decides on 128-bit values.
- The dispatch machinery here (cached state per library, enif_getenv override, __defk_stats__ report, inline asm so it inlines without the target feature) generalises: one state per builtin family (crc, pmull, aes, sha2).

title: Prototype: hardware-instruction builtins with exact meanings (crc32c first)
